claims.claim: Variability of trips in the long-delay condition in Experiment 2a
claims.tolerance: Equality at the precision printed in the article; conventional rounding.
claims.cause: A descriptive SD is mistyped in the published article.
claims.evidence: https://osf.io/download/k6xce/ — §2 Computational Reproducibility, PDF p. 3: “outputs SD = 1.14”.
claims.rationale: The final published PDF, p. 27, prints 0.14; the source reports that the original analytical script yields 1.14. This is a secondary numerical reporting discrepancy even though the report calls the main analyses reproduced.
claims.reference_evidence: https://osf.io/download/k6xce/ — §2 Computational Reproducibility, PDF p. 3: “outputs SD = 1.14”.
claims.second_labeller_rationale: The printed SD (0.14) differs from the unchanged code's 1.14; under R2 a wrong descriptive number is P2.

notes.sol: Drawn as reproducible, but independent labelling identifies the source-documented secondary discrepancy. The accessible accepted manuscript prints 1.14; the final SAGE PDF prints 0.14 and is the reported-value target. Trial coding and revised model specifications do not enter the verdict.
notes.claude: C1 is P2 under R2 (a wrong descriptive SD, 0.14 vs 1.14). No paper alternative under R7: a confirmed wrong printed number rules out 'computationally reproducible'. Reconciled with the second labeller (see reconciliation.md). The final judgement is the structured label; notes_blind_original keeps the pre-reconciliation blind notes, which are historical and superseded wherever they conflict with the final label.
notes.claude_blind_original_historical: C1 is exactly the typo'd value the report flags (paper SD = 0.14, script SD = 1.14), so the claim list deliberately includes the one non-recurring output. By the letter of the rules (printed number wrong, unchanged code gives a different value) C1 is discrepant and the paper is 'computational issues'; the report's own verdict is 'we successfully reached computational reproducibility from raw data', hence 'computationally reproducible' as an acceptable alternative. Severity: P3 chosen because it is a typo in a descriptive SD with no effect on tests; P2 (wrong secondary descriptive statistic) is also defensible. Report gives no recomputed numbers for C2-C6; label rests on its blanket statement. Report notes 'Trial' coded as integer only in unreported models (not relevant). Robustness section ignored.
